copper_E_lower_MPa.note: lower end of annealed copper modulus, used only for the strands-only buckling load (friction check); not used for any retention bound

copper_density_g_cm3.note: reference value for the cable weight bound

cut_length_tolerance_mm.note: +/- on the design length after crimping; drives the former height and the slack bound; to be measured (M34-03, M-09)

former_clearance_mm.note: the former (inner block under the top leg, corners at the bend inner surface) is a contact guide surface in the arch plane; it stops the arch from sagging and the bends from tightening. Its height is set at assembly (former_setting_resolution_mm)

former_setting_resolution_mm.note: the former height is set at assembly (and after any harness replacement) so the top leg rests on it: lowered, then raised until it touches and locked (shim or captive screw). The remaining gap is at most this value, so at most twice it of slack can move into a free span; without the setting step the cut tolerance and the board bow leave 2.28 mm of slack (sensitivity)

friction_coefficient_upper.note: upper bound for insulation on a radiused guide surface; not measured (M34-04)

grip_length_design_mm.note: bundle length kept free for a two-finger grip above the fan-in during a 15 mm withdrawal (JST: hold the wire in a bundle within 15 degrees); the maker grip length gh_bundle_grip_length_mm stays UNCONFIRMED

guide_clearance_mm.note: radial play between the dressed bundle envelope (JST maximum OD + 0.25 mm dressing) and each guide wall, sleeve bore, end wall and cap; out-of-plane movement inside RG34 is bounded by this value

guide_closure_gap_max_mm.note: largest gap at a lid or sleeve parting line when closed on its positive stop; must stay below half the smallest wire OD so no conductor can enter (pinch) or pass (escape)

guide_edge_radius_mm.note: every edge a conductor can touch (sleeve ends, channel entries, lid edges) is radiused; insulation protection

guide_fab_tolerance_mm.note: profile tolerance of RG34 surfaces; no part exists

guide_mount_float_mm.note: RG34 post to crossmember:rear:0 fastening float; no fastener selected

guide_wall_mm.note: wall, lid, cap and sleeve thickness (machined 6061-T6 with radiused cable edges, or an equivalent part)

insulation_density_upper_g_cm3.note: PTFE-class upper value so the cable weight is an upper bound for any insulation

inter_carrier_registration_mm.note: the carriers bolt to enclosure cleats that are not designed; actual registration unknown (M34-06)

registration_allowance_mm.note: REQUIREMENT, not a known value: largest relative position error between the rear carrier (RG34, core) and the jack/middle carriers (housings) that the design tolerates; sets the free length below each sleeve for an S-bend at the maker radius

Connector service (one end at a time): Power off; remove the rear cover. The core may stay installed.
Open and remove only the sleeve of the end to be serviced; the channel, its lid and the other sleeve stay closed.

Press the latch, hold the bundle in the grip zone above the fan-in and pull within 15 degrees of +z; the cable slides through the channel and the opposite sleeve and the arch rises inside the channel (cap above the single-end raised top).
Re-mate along -z, pulling the arch back down onto the former; refit the sleeve and check its stop.
Never withdraw both ends of one cable with the lid closed: the raised arch would hit the cap (blocked by design). For harness replacement open the lid and both sleeves first.
Core service (unchanged order): Power off; remove the rear cover.
Disconnect K-PWR, release the four core screws and withdraw the core 40 mm along +z. RG34 and both arches stay in place; the J-PWR channel wall, not the cable, faces the core volume.
Front jack board removal: Power off; remove the rear cover; open both lids and all four sleeves; unmate both middle ends and lift both cables out of their channels.

Remove RG34 (J-SIG channel from the J-PWR channel, then the J-PWR channel and post from crossmember:rear:0): the A01-jack M3/M4 screwdriver columns are used only with RG34 removed (the J-PWR channel is within K4 of the M4 column).
Lift each free middle end back over the A01-middle edge to x < 232 and remove the front panel assembly as in Stage10 with the cables attached to A01-jack.
Harness replacement: Power off; remove the rear cover; open both lids and all four sleeves.
Unmate the middle ends, then the local ends, from the rear; lift each cable out of its channel. No board, carrier or the core is removed.
Fit the new harness as in RG34 assembly, setting both formers again.
RG34 assembly: Fit carriers, boards and the core as in Stage10; fit the RG34 post on crossmember:rear:0 (proposal).

From the rear (cover off): mate J-PWR at both ends, dress it into one arch and lay it into the J-PWR channel; set the J-PWR former (lower it, raise it until the top leg rests on it, gap <= former_setting_resolution_mm, lock it); close the J-PWR lid and both J-PWR sleeves.
Mate J-SIG at both ends, fit the J-SIG channel to the J-PWR channel, lay J-SIG in, set its former the same way, close its lid and both sleeves.
Check that each lid and sleeve sits on its stop (closure gap <= guide_closure_gap_max_mm) with no conductor in a parting line; refit the rear cover.
